solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Language once right to be used in hospital burlesque?

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: something used in a word is placed inside it, so the right letter goes into the burlesque

parts.note: a skit is a burlesque or comic parody

explanation.surface: A question about whether a word meaning 'right' crops up in some hospital comedy sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical tongue of ancient India is no longer spoken in everyday life, so it is a language of the past.

clue.text: Heather's personal introduction to New Statesman?

parts.note: heather is the plant genus Erica, so a girl named Erica introducing herself says '(I) am Erica'

explanation.surface: Heather writes a self-introduction for a political weekly, the New Statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Statesman is a British political magazine; the question mark flags that 'Statesman' is to be read as a man of the (United) States.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the United States can whimsically be called a man of the States.

clue.text: Adults may have them, not only children

definitions.text: Adults may have them, not only children

parts.words: Adults may have them, not only children
parts.note: brothers and sisters are often thought of as a childhood matter, but grown-ups have them too; 'not only children' also hints at someone who is not an only child

explanation.surface: A remark about something grown-ups possess as well as youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not only children' doubles as 'not only-children': people who have brothers or sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothers and sisters remain family whatever age they reach, so grown-ups as well as youngsters have them.

clue.text: Reportedly regretted being cross

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone, so it is said, was sorry for being angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective (angry) but is the noun: a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is an old word for the cross of Christ, especially one set above a church screen.

clue.text: Structural member that is black, secured by gang

indicators.note: being secured by something means being held within it, so the gang wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a team is a gang of workers
IE is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A girder held in place by a building crew, described as black.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal timber joining the feet of rafters is a load-bearing part of a roof frame.

clue.text: Love letter in post before announcement of party?

parts.note: a billet is a posting or job, a post

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken aloud, so the party word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A love letter arrives in the mail ahead of an invitation to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announcement of' makes DO sound like the French DOUX.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'sweet note', is borrowed in English for a romantic message.

clue.text: Good person going over route for flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over places the saint above the route

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
an airway is a route used by aircraft

explanation.surface: A kind traveller checks the route for an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, as 'route' encourages; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is a series of stairs between floors.

clue.text: Splendid publicity inspiring duke's older relative

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the duke is taken inside

parts.note: grand means splendid
an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity
D is the abbreviation for duke; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Wonderful advertising breathes life into an aristocrat's elderly kinsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's father is an elder member of one's family.

clue.text: Mimic — one getting duty list backed by Cambridge college

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the duty list is read in reverse

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A copycat is handed a duty roster supported by a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge college' points to Cambridge, England; it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. 'backed' makes ATOR from ROTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copies the speech or manner of others is a copier, the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Quiet English male lacking funds in Welsh town

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: A quiet, penniless Englishman finds himself in a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in Pembrokeshire, south-west Wales, known for its castle.

clue.text: South American girl within borders of Bahrain

indicators.note: within says the girl's name sits inside the border letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman from South America is found living inside Bahrain's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Bolivia, a landlocked country in South America, is a South American.

clue.text: Image-breaker's current scam finally taking in old clubs

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the run of current, scam and finally wraps around the other letters

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a con is a scam
last means finally, as in 'at last'
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A smasher of images is finally caught after a fraud involving antique golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts OC between ICON and LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant one who destroyed religious images, from Greek for 'image-breaker'.

clue.text: Messy train woman brought round to disinfect

indicators.note: the woman is brought round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: Chloe is a woman's name

indicators.note: messy says the letters of train are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dirty train carrying a fainted woman who has been revived must be sanitised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' reads as reviving someone who fainted; here the woman's name wraps around the jumbled letters RINAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding a chemical such as that used in swimming pools kills germs in water.

clue.text: A day to be overcome with wonder!

parts.note: Wed is short for Wednesday, a day

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a day can leave one amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck with reverence or amazement is to be filled with admiring fear.

clue.text: Felons surprisingly collecting drug personally

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the drug goes inside
surprisingly signals the letters of felons turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: Criminals unexpectedly pick up narcotics for their own use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' gives ONESLF from FELONS; 'collecting' takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oneself means doing it in person, by your own hand.

clue.text: Big guns knight invited into ranker's function

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or rankers

indicators.note: something invited into a place goes inside it

parts.note: a dance is a social function
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is invited to an army private's social, where cannons are on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Military artillery collectively, heavy cannons and the like, is the meaning here.

clue.text: They choose English readers in foreign universities

parts.note: a lector is a lecturer or reader at a university, especially abroad

explanation.surface: English-language lecturers working at overseas universities get to pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters are people who select candidates at the ballot box.

clue.text: Flush individual received by brother and journalist

indicators.note: received by means taken inside, so the individual goes into the exclamation

parts.note: 'Brother!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise
one is a single individual
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A single person blushing at a meeting with a sibling and a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush is slang for having plenty of cash, which is to be wealthy.

clue.text: Old bird and bloke outside

parts.note: ex means former, old
a tern is a seabird
Al is a man's name, any bloke

explanation.surface: An ageing bird and a man are out in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the outer side or surface is the opposite of internal.

clue.text: Stretch limo originally acceptable in key northern street

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the key and street

parts.note: E is a musical key
gate is a word for street in northern English place names, as in York

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of limo

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A long limousine, perfectly fine, parked in an important northern street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch limo' is a tempting phrase; 'Stretch' alone is the definition. 'in' puts LON inside E GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something, pulling it out, is to make it longer.

clue.text: Man about town — Ronnie Winslow, for example?

definitions.meaning: a wealthy pleasure-seeking man who lives for society and parties
Ronnie Winslow is the boy in Rattigan's play The Winslow Boy, so he is a boy from a play

explanation.walkthrough: The Winslow Boy is Terence Rattigan's 1946 play about a cadet wrongly accused of theft; the question mark flags the split into PLAY + BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich man devoted to pleasure and society life is a classic man about town.

clue.text: Buy it, trying at first to control weight

parts.note: to buy it is slang for to die

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of trying

explanation.surface: Advice to purchase a product, trying it out first, as a way to manage weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy it' is slang for being killed, not shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricting what you eat in order to slim is the verb sense of going on a regime.

clue.text: Kinsman keeping US chopper for leisure

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the kinsman wraps around the chopper

parts.note: a relation is a kinsman
ax is the American spelling of the chopping tool

explanation.surface: A relative holding on to an American helicopter as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter; it is an axe, spelt the US way.
explanation.definitionFit: Time spent unwinding and resting is free time, ease from work.

clue.text: Advocate a change of course for speakers extremely eagerly

indicators.note: for speakers means as heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a turn is a change of course

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of eagerly

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly urges a change of direction for those giving speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for speakers' makes A TURN sound like ATTORN; the ends of eagerly give EY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who pleads a case in court is an advocate, the American term for counsel.

clue.text: Sharp girl about to go climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: A clever young woman is about to set off for the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart or biting taste or comment is called sour or cutting, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Like some philosophy a politician initially imparted in bar

indicators.note: in means put inside, so the pieces go into the word for bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar
CON is short for Conservative, a politician

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of imparted

explanation.surface: A politician first explains some philosophy in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon's school of thought, based on empirical inquiry, gives the adjective for related ideas.

clue.text: In small shelter rent out old historical wind instrument

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the shelter

parts.note: a cot is a small shelter, as in a dovecot

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone inside a little hut lets out an antique instrument for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent out' reads as letting a property; 'out' alone is the anagram signal, giving RNET.
explanation.definitionFit: This Renaissance instrument is a wooden horn with finger holes and a cup mouthpiece.

clue.text: Vocalist's slangy greeting to famous countertenor

parts.note: yo is a slang greeting
Alfred Deller was a celebrated English countertenor

explanation.surface: A singer greets a well-known countertenor with street slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of the Alpine warbling style switching between chest voice and falsetto is a kind of singer.
